title: Adaptive connection hints and streamer ergonomics for cross-SDK transports
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a cross-SDK strategy for adaptive connection hints, safe socket reuse, and improved streaming ergonomics. The goal is to reduce tail-latency and connection churn for typical Redwood workloads (short requests mixed with streaming chat) while keeping SDK defaults ergonomic for application developers.

Motivation and context: Current SDK defaults work for most cases but show increased reconnects, subtle streaming reconnect edge cases, and suboptimal interaction with server-side batching. Different languages have different network stacks and semantics (Python asyncio vs Node HTTP/2 vs Go net/http). We want one coherent policy: per-route connection profiles, adaptive idle/reuse heuristics, and streaming client APIs that surface safe reconnection semantics and backpressure hints. This ticket covers design, conservative defaults, and end-to-end examples for Python, TypeScript, and Go.

Scope:
- Define a compact set of "connection hint" profiles (low-latency, balanced, high-throughput, streaming-heavy) and map to transport parameters per SDK.
- Expose an ergonomic streaming API pattern that clarifies reconnection semantics and provides explicit drain and resume hooks.
- Implement adaptive socket reuse heuristics to avoid premature connection close while preventing unbounded TCP reuse in long-lived processes.
- Add examples and README snippets for Python/TS/Go showing recommended config for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Add telemetry events for reconnects, idle-prune triggers, and streaming resume failures to inform future tuning.

Out of scope for this ticket: kernel-level optimizations, server-side scheduling changes, and dedicated autoscaler policy changes.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Use conservative defaults that favor stability for first-party customers; opt-in more aggressive pooling for Dedicated customers via explicit profile.
- Prefer explicit developer-facing API to magic heuristics: SDKs will provide a small typed enum for profile + optional fine-tune parameters for advanced users.
- Avoid per-request global deadline overrides; instead recommend per-route settings applied at client creation or per-call binding to keep semantics predictable across streaming and non-streaming calls.
- Telemetry will be minimal at GA (counts & rates) and extended later if we see signal.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Spec document committed describing profiles, mapping table per-language, and API examples.
2) SDK PRs in Python, TypeScript, and Go with default config implemented and unit tests covering: connection hint selection, idle prune behavior, and a streaming reconnect unit (mocked server).
3) Example app for each language demonstrating chat streaming with graceful cancel/resume and a short-run benchmark showing at least 15% reduction in reconnects for mixed short+stream workload on hosted environment.
4) Telemetry events emitted: reconnect_attempt, reconnect_success, idle_prune, streaming_resume_error.
5) Console doc page draft submitted linking the SDK examples and runtime knobs.

Risks and mitigations:
- Language-specific network semantics could cause behavior divergence: mitigate by a compatibility matrix in the spec and requiring smoke tests across languages.
- Overly aggressive reuse could hide server-side load balancing issues: mitigate by providing an explicit profile for Dedicated deployments tuned to expected throughput and by observing telemetry for error spikes.
- Streaming reconnection complexity may confuse app developers: mitigate by documenting explicitly when reconnection is safe and by providing an easy opt-in streaming resume API with example code.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge spec and code behind feature flag in SDKs (alpha).
2) Internal dogfood: use the new defaults in staging and a small set of internal services for two weeks.
3) Collect telemetry, iterate on heuristics.
4) Flip default for new SDK minor release and publish migration guide.

Long-term: consider adding adaptive server-sent hints for idle thresholds and integrate with Redwood Optimize to recommend per-client profile based on historical traffic patterns.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Spec doc in repo: transport_profiles.md committed. 2) SDK PRs for python/ts/go implementing defaults + tests. 3) Three example apps demonstrating streaming ergonomics. 4) Telemetry events: reconnect_attempt|reconnect_success|idle_prune|streaming_resume_error. 5) Console doc page draft linked in attachments.
steps: 1) Draft transport_profiles.md and per-language mapping table. 2) Review with SDK leads (Python: Lina Gomez, TS: Mateo Ruiz, Go: Omar Farouk). 3) Implement feature-flagged defaults in three SDKs. 4) Add unit/integration tests, example apps, and telemetry hooks. 5) Dogfood and iterate, update docs, flip flag and ship.
notes:
Per-language nuances: Python asyncio needs explicit connection pool size + keepalive timer; Node should prefer HTTP/2 session reuse with maxConcurrentStreams tuning; Go should expose Transport.DialContext wrapper and control MaxIdleConnsPerHost. We will provide recommended numeric presets in the spec but keep them conservative for hosted tier.

Presets (initial draft):
- low-latency: max_idle_conns=2, idle_timeout=2s, max_per_host=6, aggressive_reconnect=false
- balanced: max_idle_conns=8, idle_timeout=10s, max_per_host=32, aggressive_reconnect=false
- high-throughput: max_idle_conns=64, idle_timeout=60s, max_per_host=200, aggressive_reconnect=true
- streaming-heavy: max_idle_conns=16, idle_timeout=30s, max_per_host=64, streaming_resume_buffer=64KB

These numbers are placeholders for discussion and tests.
